title: Report a vehicle sold, disposed of or moved away (personal property tax)
question: I sold my car or moved out of Albemarle. How do I stop being taxed?
office: Department of Finance & Budget, Office of Revenue Administration (Business & Personal Tax Unit), County of Albemarle. Under the county executive form there is no elected Commissioner of the Revenue or Treasurer: the Director of Finance assesses, bills, collects and refunds the tax (Va. Code §§ 15.2-521, 15.2-522).
summary: Albemarle prorates vehicle tax by month, so you stop owing for the months after you sell, trade, junk or move a vehicle away, once the records show it. First tell Virginia DMV: report the sale, surrender the title of a junked vehicle, deal with the plates, or update your address and garage jurisdiction. Then tell the Office of Revenue Administration by phone, email, fax or mail. After a move to another state, send a copy of the new registration within 30 days; until it arrives the county keeps taxing. A move to a Virginia locality that does not prorate leaves you taxed through December 31. Keep paying bills, and ask in writing for a correction if one is wrong.

steps.step: Sold, traded or donated the vehicle: sign the title over and tell Virginia DMV yourself
steps.who: Vehicle owner (seller), with the Virginia Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)
steps.how: Sign the title over to the buyer and give it to them: every owner on the title signs, and you fill in the buyer's name and address, the odometer reading, the date of sale and the price (or "gift"). Then report the sale, trade or donation to DMV online, at a DMV customer service center or by phone. The county page gives DMV's number as (804) 497-7100. Do this yourself: the county warns not to rely on the buyer or the dealer. The county bases the tax, and any refund, on the sale date as updated with DMV, so a late DMV report can mean more months of tax.
steps.deadline: as soon as possible (county FAQ). The county's Purchasing and Selling page cites Va. Code § 46.2-600 for notifying DMV within thirty days of a purchase or transfer; that section sets the 30 days for the owner's title application. Va. Code § 46.2-604, which makes the seller notify DMV, sets no time limit.

steps.step: Take off the license plates, then reuse them or turn them in
steps.how: Remove the plates before the buyer takes the vehicle. You can move them to a replacement vehicle. If you will not reuse them, turn them in or inactivate them online, or at a DMV customer service center or DMV Select, before you tell your insurance company about the sale. DMV warns that if your insurer cancels coverage before DMV knows of the sale, its records show an uninsured registered vehicle, and it may suspend your driver's license and registration privileges. If six months or more are left on the registration, you may get part of the registration fee back: mail form FMS-210 (f3) with the plates, or hand both in at a customer service center or DMV Select. DMV mails the refund to the address it has on file, so update your address first; the form says to write to the DMV Refund Section if the check has not arrived within 30 days.
steps.deadline: a registration refund needs six or more full months left in the registration period (Va. Code § 46.2-688; form FMS 210)
steps.fee: a prorated registration refund, in six-month increments, carries no charge or deduction (Va. Code § 46.2-688); form FMS 210 says DMV deducts a $5.00 processing fee only if none of the registration period has passed; partial refunds do not include one-time plate reservation fees, Virginia Road Tax for heavy trucks or late fees (DMV page)
steps.quote: The seller should remove the license plates from the vehicle before allowing the buyer to take possession of the vehicle

steps.step: Junked or totaled the vehicle: surrender the title to DMV
steps.how: Surrender the title to DMV if you have it. If you no longer have the title, tell DMV that the vehicle has been junked. Then contact the county's Office of Revenue Administration (step s6). The county's refund or adjustment follows the salvage date recorded with DMV. The county's tax guide lists a vehicle that was sold, purchased, junked or totaled among the changes to report on its tax adjustments line, 434-296-5852.

steps.step: Moved to another Virginia city or county: give DMV your new address, garage jurisdiction and move date
steps.who: Vehicle owner, with Virginia DMV; then the Office of Revenue Administration
steps.how: Tell DMV your new address, the locality where the vehicle is now garaged and the date you moved. DMV asks for your full name and customer number, and the title number and last 4 digits of the VIN for each vehicle. Then contact the county (step s6). If your new locality prorates, Albemarle's tax stops at the move (step s7). If it does not prorate, Albemarle keeps taxing the vehicle through December 31 of the year you moved, and state law bars a refund for the rest of that year. The county does not list which localities do not prorate; ask your new locality.
steps.deadline: within 30 days of the move (Va. Code § 46.2-606(A))
steps.fee: DMV may charge $5 if you do not report the address change (Va. Code § 46.2-606(D))

steps.step: Moved to another state: register the vehicle there and send the county proof
steps.who: Vehicle owner, to the new state's motor vehicle agency and to the Office of Revenue Administration
steps.how: Register or title the vehicle in your new state. Then send the Office of Revenue Administration a copy of the new state's title or registration that clearly shows the date the vehicle was registered there. If you sold or traded the vehicle after the move without registering it in the new state, send a copy of the bill of sale showing the Vehicle Identification Number and the date of the sale instead. Send it by fax (434-243-7906), email (Tax@Albemarle.org) or mail (step s6). The county says the vehicle stays taxable here until that evidence reaches its office. DMV encourages you to return the Virginia plates by mail once the vehicle is re-registered (or surrender them online); it says this is not required, but do not cancel your Virginia insurance before the plates are surrendered. If six full months or more remain on the Virginia registration, mail form FMS-210 (f3) with the plates for a refund.
steps.deadline: within 30 days of your move, as the county asks (Moving Personal Property page and FAQ); no penalty for missing it was found, but the county keeps taxing the vehicle until the proof reaches its office

steps.step: Tell the Office of Revenue Administration, with proof of the date
steps.who: Vehicle owner, to the Department of Finance & Budget, Office of Revenue Administration (Business & Personal Tax Unit)
steps.how: The county asks to be told about every move, in or out, and its Purchasing and Selling page says to contact the Office of Revenue Administration after you have contacted DMV, so that it can update your account and adjust your billing. No separate county form for reporting a sale or disposal was found. Contact the Business & Personal Tax Unit by phone (434-296-5852), email (Tax@Albemarle.org), fax (434-243-7906) or mail (County of Albemarle, Revenue Administration, 401 McIntire Road, Room 133, Charlottesville, VA 22902), in person on the 1st floor of the County Office Building (Monday to Friday, 8 am to 5 pm, except holidays), or book an appointment online. Identify yourself, your account and the vehicle, and give the date it was sold, junked or moved. The county asks for documents only after a move to another state (the new registration, or a bill of sale showing the VIN and the date; step s5); for a sale or junking it goes by the DMV record, so keep your bill of sale or DMV receipt in case the date is questioned. The county's tax guide also says you can notify it by submitting a Personal Property Registration form (f2, or the online version f4); the paper form's fields are for a vehicle coming into the county (purchase date, date the vehicle entered the county, former residence), and it has no field for a sale, disposal or move-out date.
steps.deadline: none stated for a sale or junking; within 30 days of a move to another state (step s5)

steps.step: The county ends the tax by the month
steps.who: Department of Finance & Budget, Office of Revenue Administration (the Director of Finance holds the commissioner of the revenue's powers, Va. Code § 15.2-521)
steps.how: Albemarle prorates. A vehicle is taxed from the date it is bought or registered with DMV as garaged in the county until the date it is retitled elsewhere, sold, junked, or taken to another prorating Virginia locality. Under state law more than half a month counts as a full month, and less than half a month is not counted. The end date used: for a sale or trade, the sale date as updated with DMV; for a junked vehicle, the salvage date recorded with DMV; for a move to another state, the new state's registration date, but the county also says tax continues until the proof reaches its office; for a move to a non-prorating Virginia locality, December 31. Months for which another Virginia locality legally assessed the vehicle and the tax was paid are exempt here.
steps.fee: tax at 4.28% of assessed value ($4.28 per $100) for calendar year 2026, less car tax relief on qualifying vehicles, for the months the vehicle had its situs in the county

steps.step: Get the refund or credit, or a corrected bill
steps.who: Department of Finance & Budget, Office of Revenue Administration (the Director of Finance holds the treasurer's powers, Va. Code § 15.2-522)
steps.how: If you already paid for months after the vehicle left, state law has the prorated tax refunded to you or credited against tax on another vehicle you own in the same tax year. A refund under $5 is issued only if you ask for it, and the county is not required to pay interest on a refund that results from proration. If the bill is not yet paid, the county relieves the months that are not owed. A change made after billing can come as a supplemental bill, which has its own due date. No county page says how or when refunds are paid; for payments, balances and supplemental bills the office lists 434-296-5851 and payments@albemarle.org.
steps.deadline: a refund is due within thirty days of the date the tax is relieved (Va. Code § 58.1-3516(A))
steps.quote: Such refund shall be made within thirty days of the date such tax is relieved.

steps.step: Keep paying any bill by its due date while the change is processed
steps.who: Vehicle owner (pays); Office of Revenue Administration (bills and collects)
steps.how: Bills are due June 25 and December 5; a due date on a weekend moves to the next business day. The county's penalty policy says penalty and interest are not waived because a bill was incorrect, was not received or was mailed to the wrong address. Pay on time, or get the bill corrected before the due date; once the change is made, an overpayment is refunded or credited (step s8). Unpaid taxes can lead to a DMV registration hold, tax liens, debt set-off and referral to a collection agency. Pay online at albemarlecountytaxes.org, by phone at 866-820-5450, by mail, at the 24/7 kiosk or in person. If you asked in writing for a correction within 90 days of the assessment, state law says the bill is not treated as delinquent, or sent to collection, while the request is pending and for 30 days after the decision; interest can still be charged on any part found to be owed (see the escalation routes).
steps.deadline: June 25 and December 5; a supplemental bill has its own due date
steps.fee: late-payment penalty of 10 percent (at least $10) on each assessed item; interest of 10% a year (Albemarle County Code §§ 15-103(A), 15-104, as stated by the county)

steps.step: If the bill is still wrong, ask in writing for a correction
steps.who: Vehicle owner, to the Department of Finance & Budget (the assessing official)
steps.how: If the disposal date or the address on the bill is wrong, call the tax adjustments line (434-296-5852) first. If that does not fix it, write to the Department of Finance & Budget asking for a correction of the assessment. The county lists no required contents for a correction request. Its appeal-rights notice (f1) says an administrative appeal (the route for local business taxes and for trailers, boats, campers and other local mobile property) must contain the taxpayer's name and address, federal tax identification number, local tax account number, a power of attorney or letter of representation if someone else applies, a copy of the assessment, a detailed explanation of the taxpayer's position and a statement of the relief requested, sent to Department of Finance & Budget, Attn: Revenue Administration - Assessments Unit, 401 McIntire Road, Room 133, Charlottesville, VA 22902. Those contents, with your proof (DMV record, bill of sale or new registration), are a sensible guide for a correction request too. You may ask for the facts and law behind the decision in writing (Va. Code § 58.1-3981(F)). The county says you can go to the Circuit Court at any point. See the escalation routes.
steps.deadline: within three years from the last day of the tax year, or within one year from the date of the assessment, whichever is later (Va. Code § 58.1-3980(A)); an unpaid bill for a year in which you were not subject to the tax may be challenged while it is collectible (Va. Code § 58.1-3980(B))

caveats: Albemarle County's website (www.albemarle.org) refuses automated readers, so the county pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them before you act. The DMV pages were read live. The County's Terms and Conditions bar reposting its content without written permission, so the County's own words are not reprinted on this page; each step links the County page instead.

No county disposal form. Unlike Charlottesville, Albemarle publishes no form for reporting a vehicle sold, junked or moved away that was found. Its pages ask you to contact the Office of Revenue Administration by phone, email, fax or mail, and its tax guide says you can also notify it with the Personal Property Registration form (f2). The county's online registration form (forms.office.com) refuses automated readers, so its fields are not described here. No fee for reporting a change was found. Two editions of the paper registration form are linked: the Moving Personal Property page (May 2026 snapshot) links f2, and the Personal Property Taxes & Fees page (August 2026 snapshot) links an older edition (showpublisheddocument/8231) and the online form (f4).

Deadlines. The only county deadline found is 30 days after a move to another state, for sending the new state's registration. For a sale or junking the county gives none (its FAQ says to tell DMV as soon as possible). The Purchasing and Selling page says Va. Code § 46.2-600 requires notifying DMV within thirty days of purchase or transfer, but that section puts the 30-day duty on the owner applying for a title; § 46.2-604, which makes the seller notify DMV, sets no time limit. The registration form cites County Code § 15-801 for a new return when status changes (compare Va. Code § 58.1-3518.1(B)); the text of § 15-801, and any deadline or penalty in it, were not read.

Which date ends the tax differs between county pages. For a sale, the FAQ uses the date the sale was updated with DMV and the Purchasing and Selling page uses the date DMV received the information, not necessarily the actual sale date. For a move to another state, the Moving page asks for registration that shows the date the vehicle was registered in the new state, while the FAQ says taxation ceases once the copy has been provided, and the guide says vehicles remain taxable until evidence of registration is received. If the county uses a later date than your documents show, ask for a correction (step s10).

Statute attribution. The county's Moving page and tax guide say that under Va. Code § 58.1-3511 vehicles remain taxable until evidence of new registration is provided (the guide misprints the citation as §58.3511). The section as indexed does not say that in terms. The closest rule is § 58.1-3511(A)(i): a vehicle of 10,000 pounds or less registered in Virginia but garaged in another state has its situs where it is registered in Virginia. The evidence rule appears to be county practice built on that.

Local ordinance not checked. Albemarle's tax guide says the county is a pro-rating locality, and its pages describe monthly proration, but the ordinance adopting proration under Va. Code § 58.1-3516 (County Code Chapter 15, Article 8, from § 15-800) has not been checked. The Code of Ordinances is on Municode, whose CivicPlus terms forbid automated access and copying. Legistar's matter records and staff reports give no proposed or adopted ordinance text. The local legal_basis quotes come from county pages and the county's form, not from the Code.

Vehicle license fee on a sale or move. The guide calls the license fee an annual prorated fee, and Va. Code § 46.2-752(A) lets the locality prorate it, but no county page says whether part of the fee is refunded or credited when a vehicle is sold or moved away. Legistar matter 21-373 (2021) proposed County Code §§ 15-1405 (Prorating) and 15-1406 (Refunds) for the vehicle license tax; their text and adoption were not confirmed (the matter's history in Legistar is empty). DMV's form FMS 210 also tells applicants to contact their locality about refunds of local license fees.

Refund mechanics. No county page states how or when prorated refunds or credits are paid. The 30-day refund rule, the $5 minimum and the no-interest rule for proration refunds come from state law (Va. Code §§ 58.1-3516, 58.1-3916). A 2026 Board of Supervisors staff report (Legistar 26-344, Quarterly Tax Refund Approval Request) says refunds from erroneous assessments over $10,000 need Board approval and that the county requests them quarterly; ordinary vehicle refunds are far below that. Va. Code § 58.1-3990 (refund ordinance) was not used, because no county source showed it has been adopted.

Not everything is prorated the same way. Va. Code § 58.1-3516 covers motor vehicles, trailers, semitrailers and boats. Mobile homes classified as personal property are taxed at the real estate rate; a 2022 proposal (Legistar 22-482) to add County Code § 15-806 on proration for manufactured homes was not confirmed. Boats are registered with the Department of Wildlife Resources, and aircraft with the FAA; how to report their sale or move is not covered here. Whether the county excludes heavy interstate for-hire vehicles from proration, as § 58.1-3516(A) allows, was not found.

Non-prorating localities. The county's pages say a move to a Virginia locality that does not prorate leaves you taxed by Albemarle through December 31, and Va. Code § 58.1-3516(A) bars the refund. The county does not list which localities do not prorate. Charlottesville prorates (see curated/places/va/charlottesville/personal_property_change_report.json); Staunton was not checked.
Car tax relief (PPTR) and the PPTR percentage for 2026 were not confirmed; how relief is prorated along with the tax on a partial-year bill or refund is not stated by the county.
Town of Scottsville: the county collects the town's motor vehicle license taxes under a 2021 agreement (Legistar 21-510). How town residents' license tax is prorated or refunded is not covered here.

The Tax Commissioner appeal (Va. Code § 58.1-3983.1) covers only 'local mobile property tax' (airplanes, boats, campers, recreational vehicles and trailers) and local business taxes. For a car, pickup or motorcycle, the next step after the county is the circuit court. The county's appeal-rights sheet describes the same routes.

Contacts. The appeal-rights PDF (dated by its URL to December 2022) gives fax 434-244-4929 and a finance department mailbox, and the registration form gives tel 434-296-5851; the county's web pages give 434-296-5852 and Tax@Albemarle.org for the Business & Personal Tax Unit and fax 434-243-7906, which are recorded here. The appeal-rights PDF's mailbox is not recorded because the web pages publish Tax@Albemarle.org for this unit. The office address appears as Room 133 on the web pages and Suite 133 on the forms. The DMV online services (report a vehicle, plate surrender) are linked from DMV's pages and not described here. FMS 210 (07/01/2022 edition) has fillable fields, bases refunds on each 6 full months remaining, and deducts a $5.00 processing fee only if none of the registration period has passed. DMV's Moving Within Virginia page says to return a decal to the old locality; Albemarle no longer issues decals.

Privacy: the Circuit Court Clerk's page names the Clerk and Chief Deputy Clerk, Legistar records carry staff names and mailboxes, and some county PDFs give department mailboxes. None of these are recorded. The Clerk's page also links an old notice that the office is closed to public traffic; current hours were not confirmed.

Terms: albemarle.org's terms authorize browsing for informational purposes but require written permission to repost or redistribute site content, so page quotes are kept to one sentence or clause for citation. Republishing them on a wiki may need the county's permission.

Quotes: state-law quotes are matched to Open US Law's copy of the Code of Virginia, cut before cross-references where that copy puts a space before punctuation. Local quotes keep the county's own wording and spelling, including 'pro-rating' and 'non-prorating'. The tax guide PDF uses typographic ligatures and line-break hyphens, so quotes from it avoid words whose extracted text was ambiguous.

removed: fees, DMV registration refund: the Va. Code § 46.2-688 quote 'The Commissioner shall retain five dollars of the fee...' was the basis for 'DMV keeps $5' on a prorated refund. The quote is verbatim and stays in legal_basis, but it sits in the paragraph on plates surrendered before the registration period begins; the fee entry now quotes form FMS 210 instead.
corrections: Method: the 52 state-law quotes were matched against I.text_of for each cited section in lexflow-app-1, whitespace normalised only, and their subsections were checked by reading the section text. The 20 local and DMV quotes were matched against pages fetched read-only with the lexflow-research User-Agent. www.albemarle.org again answered HTTP 403 (robots.txt included), so the Internet Archive snapshots named in sources were fetched in raw (id_) mode a few seconds apart; the tax guide, registration form and appeal-rights PDFs were read from those snapshots with pdftotext. The DMV pages and form FMS 210 were fetched directly, 30 seconds apart as DMV's robots.txt asks. All 72 remaining quotes matched word for word.

s2 and fees: the draft said DMV keeps $5 of a prorated registration refund. Va. Code § 46.2-688 puts the five-dollar retention in the paragraph on plates surrendered before the registration period begins and says of the prorated refund 'No charge or deduction shall be assessed for any refund made under this subsection' (new legal_basis quote). Form FMS 210, now read, says the $5.00 processing fee is deducted only if none of the registration period has passed. The step, the fee entry and the deadline (six or more full months) now say so. Added from FMS 210 that the refund is mailed to the address DMV has on file and whom to write to if it has not arrived in 30 days.
fees: the DMV address-change fee was 'up to $5'; Va. Code § 46.2-606(D) says the person 'may be charged a fee of $5'. Now '$5 (DMV may charge it)'.

s8: 'no interest is paid on a refund that comes from proration' overstated Va. Code § 58.1-3916, which says no interest 'shall be required to be paid' on such a refund. Now 'the county is not required to pay interest'.

s10: the draft said an administrative appeal 'should give' a shortened list of contents. The appeal-rights notice (f1) says an administrative appeal 'must' contain them, and that route covers local license, business and mobile property taxes, not a correction request for a car. The step now says the county lists no required contents for a correction request, gives f1's full list (including federal tax identification number and power of attorney or letter of representation) and f1's mailing address for appeals, and offers the list only as a guide.
s5: the 30-day deadline is the county's request ('Please do this within 30 days'); the deadline field now says no penalty for missing it was found and that taxation continues until the proof arrives.

s6: the draft asked for proof with every report. The county asks for documents only after a move to another state; for a sale or junking it goes by the DMV record. Added the Purchasing and Selling page's instruction to contact the Office of Revenue Administration after DMV so it can update the account and adjust billing, that the registration form's fields are for a vehicle coming into the county (no field for a sale or move-out date), and the online form (new f4, not read).

s9: added the rule in Va. Code §§ 58.1-3916 and 58.1-3958 that a bill is not treated as delinquent while a correction request filed within 90 days is pending and for 30 days after the decision, with interest still possible on any part found owing.

Escalation: the collection-hold rung now says the hold is automatic (no separate request) and that interest may still be charged. The penalty-waiver rung now lists the county policy's fourth ground (lateness due solely to the fault of the Treasurer or Commissioner) and 'not knowing the deadline' among the non-grounds, and adds the 120-day period for a fiduciary from Va. Code § 58.1-3916.

Forms: FMS 210 (f3) is the 07/01/2022 edition and has fillable fields (fillable now true). Added f4, the county's online registration form, recorded but not opened because forms.office.com's robots.txt disallows general crawlers.

Fees: added the Debt Set-Off fee ($25 county fee plus the Department of Taxation's 4%) and the collection agency fee (20% of the amount collected), both quoted from the Important Dates and Deadlines page, which the draft's step s9 already named as consequences of an unpaid bill.

Caveats and sources: the contacts caveat no longer says FMS 210 was unread; the disposal-form caveat notes the two linked editions of the paper registration form and the online form; the license-fee caveat adds FMS 210's note to ask the locality about local license fee refunds. Confirmed from the pages: the Legistar 26-344 staff report (agenda date 8/19/2026) says refunds over $10,000 need Board approval and are requested quarterly; the site terms allow browsing for informational purposes and require written permission to repost.

Confirmed without change: every county, DMV and court contact (office lines, Tax@Albemarle.org and payments@albemarle.org office mailboxes, fax, mailing address, hours, the booking link, the Circuit Court Clerk's office line), the 4.28% rate and the license fee schedule, the June 25 and December 5 due dates, the penalty and interest terms, the county's proration description, and the legal routes and deadlines in escalation. No staff names or personal mailboxes are recorded.
open_issues: www.albemarle.org blocks automated requests (HTTP 403), so every county page and PDF was checked against Internet Archive snapshots from March to September 2026, not the live site. A later change (for example a new rate, fee or contact) would not show.

The County Code was not read (Municode's terms forbid automated access): the proration ordinance in Chapter 15, Article 8, and any deadline or penalty in § 15-801 for a new return when status changes, remain unknown. The steps describe the county's published practice and say the Code was not read.

No county page says whether the vehicle license fee is refunded or credited when a vehicle is sold or moved away, or how and when prorated tax refunds are paid; the steps give only what state law and the pages say.

County pages differ on the date that ends the tax (the sale date as updated with DMV, or the date DMV received the information; for a move to another state, the new registration date, or the date the proof reaches the county). The steps and caveats give both and point to the correction route.
